correctness.rationale: Affine normalization, partition into two opposing arms and central rectangle, and exact intersection-time criterion reduce the blocked event to qZ1>stZ2. A direct convolution yields the bilateral Gamma(2) difference density, proving the exact logarithmic profile. Strict derivative positivity gives unique fixed-q optimizer; strict concavity gives the tangent-sharp stability constant; positive central area gives B<1/2. A deterministic-seed standard-library checker compares formulae with independent segment interval clipping and two-product simulations and validates all tested stability inequalities. Finite tests do not prove the quantified statements.

originality.rationale: Specific novelty is the fixed deleted-area maximizer and optimal global quantified imbalance penalty for all affine parallelogram corners, with accompanying closed two-parameter formula; not polygonal Beer-index computability, convexity bounds, or generic logarithmic integration. Relevant primary literature and accessible historical claims were compared at the implication level, with incompletely retrieved sources flagged and historical priority provisional.
residual_risks: The 2022 general Beer-index algorithm was verified by abstract but its full text was inaccessible; no whole-document exclusion is claimed.

value.rationale: Beer-index loss is a natural quantitative measure of nonconvexity. At fixed deleted-area fraction the theorem determines a unique most obstructive corner shape, a sharp global stability coefficient, an exact branch crossover at one-quarter, and an optimal universal half-blocking limit, all invariant under arbitrary nonsingular affine transformations of the containing parallelogram. These facts address the natural full two-parameter family and are not arbitrary numerical slices.
